titleEn: Gentle with the Baby, Like Touching a Leaf!

pages.text: "I came to see the baby!" Sharp-eared deer Mumu bounded onto the porch. It shook with thumps. The baby lying on leaves opened wide eyes.
"I want to play with the baby, too!" Mumu plopped down and grabbed the baby's hand. "Hello! I'm Mumu!"
The baby's face crumpled. Mumu's grip was too strong. Startled, Mumu let go. "Oh? I was only saying hello..."
Quick-handed monkey Taro laid a leaf on Mumu's palm. "Can you touch this without tearing it?" Mumu stroked it very carefully.
The leaf did not tear at all. Mumu looked at their hand. "Oh! This much strength is enough. Gentle with the Baby, Like Touching a Leaf!"
Using just that much strength, Mumu lightly held a baby finger. The baby laughed and held Mumu's finger in return.
Instead of bounding, Mumu walked softly on the porch. Turning their ears, Mumu heard the baby's gentle breathing. "That's the sound of sleeping," Mumu whispered.
Raindrops dripped from the eaves. Mumu caught one on a leaf. Gently tilting it on the porch beside the baby made the drop roll. The baby kicked little feet.
Beside a baby: one, walk softly on the porch! Two, hold the baby's hand gently, like a leaf! Three, let go if the baby frowns! Mumu stepped softly off the porch to leave, too.

Taro put an arm around Mumu's shoulders and hugged them. Using only enough strength to keep a leaf whole made the baby smile. "Can I come tomorrow? Gentle with the Baby, Like Touching a Leaf!" Mumu opened wide the hand that had stroked the leaf.
